Do you hear that? The constant gunfire? The shelling? And they tell the world there is a ceasefire? There is no pause. No reprieve. No safety for Palestinians in Gaza. On October 11, our team visited families whose tents had been burned, leaving them without shelter once again. Even as we filmed, heavy gunfire echoed around us. This is the reality of life in Gaza. Families who have lost everything continue to live under the threat of violence, yet refuse to be driven from their land. This is what steadfastness looks like. Sumud. A determination that is difficult to comprehend unless you understand what it means to face the loss of your homeland. They have burned their shelters, destroyed their neighborhoods, and displaced them again and again. But they have not broken their connection to Palestine. They are not leaving. They are not surrendering their right to exist on their land. Help support them. The Sameer Project is one of the only organizations that delivers aid in these danger zones. Give to our Food and Water Campaign .

Votes are still being counted in Israel's first election since 7 October 2023, with no clear winner yet determined. But, exit polls and partial official results show that Palestinian parties will dramatically increase their representation in the Israeli Knesset. Predictions are they could win as many as 19 seats, making them the kingmakers in negotiations to form a new government. While neither the current prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition, nor the opposition bloc led by the former general Gadi Eisenkot, have won enough seats, experts have said that if Eisenkot falls short of a majority, he would be obliged to sit down to talk with the Palestinian groupings, the Joint List and Ra’am, to try to form a government, which could take weeks. Most of the Jewish opposition parties in the Change bloc anchored by Eisenkot have rejected the idea of working with Palestinian-Israeli parties. "The big gains made by Palestinian parties in Israel’s general election pose an urgent and fundamental challenge to the country’s mainstream opposition: either cooperate with Arab Israelis or hand Benjamin Netanyahu a roadmap to political survival," writes the Guardian’s senior international correspondent, Julian Borger. Read more about how the rise of Palestinian parties will “redraw Israel's political landscape” via the link in bio.
